anya: Quick report: importing the Python SDK inside a multiprocessing child (spawn or forkserver) can crash the child with RuntimeError: There is no current event loop. Happened in a customer sample app.

kevin: yikes. which runtime? uvloop? linux only?

anya: Ubuntu 22.04, py3.10 and py3.11, no uvloop. Repro is deterministic with start_method='spawn'. Stack trace from the child: 

anya: ```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/worker.py", line 10, in <module>
    from redwood import AsyncClient
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/async_client.py", line 34, in <module>
    _loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
RuntimeError: There is no current event loop
```

marc: looks like we call get_event_loop() at module import time to seed some thread-local state. That breaks in spawn/forkserver since child processes start with a blank asyncio context.

kevin: minimal repro would help. can you share a tiny script so we can add a test?

anya: sure, here's the simplest repro we used: 

anya: ```python
# spawn_repro.py
from multiprocessing import set_start_method, Process
set_start_method('spawn')

# Import triggers the error during module import in child
from redwood import AsyncClient

def run_child():
    c = AsyncClient()
    print('child ok')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    p = Process(target=run_child)
    p.start()
    p.join()
```

marc: thanks. short-term patch: wrap asyncio.get_event_loop() in try/except and default to None. Long-term: remove import-time event loop interaction and lazy-init in AsyncClient or a module-level ensure_loop() that runs inside the child main thread.

kevin: agreed. I'll open a small hotfix PR that does the try/except for the next patch release, and a follow-up refactor PR that moves loop setup into AsyncClient._ensure_event_loop().

anya: can we also add a CI matrix job that runs the tiny spawn test under py310/py311 on linux? It's quick and would catch regressions.

infra-bot: New issue opened: REDWOOD-4921 (python-sdk: avoid import-time asyncio.get_event_loop() to support multiprocessing spawn/forkserver)

marc: also update the onboarding docs note: "avoid top-level SDK import in multiprocessing child when using spawn/forkserver" until hotfix lands. We'll remove it once refactor is merged.

kevin: will add unit + integration tests: unit to assert module import doesn't raise under spawn, and an integration probed by CI job. Also add a small whats-new blurb for the patch.

anya: I pushed the repro and test to a branch. PTAL @kevin when you open the hotfix.

infra-bot: CI passed for branch hotfix/avoid-import-loop (linux/py311).

kevin: merged hotfix. Follow-up refactor PR incoming.

anya: thanks all. leaving a snippet for docs and a note to product that some sample apps used top-level import patterns that will need tweaks (very small).

marc: closing this thread after follow-up refactor lands. thanks for catching this early!
